item.title: Book Launch: That Directionless Light of the Future, Rediscovering Russell FitzGerald — Thu Nov 26, 5:00 PM — Art Metropole
item.description:
Please join us for a book launch of That Directionless Light of the Future: Rediscovering Russell FitzGerald with editor Jon Davies. Stop by to pick up a copy of the publication and enjoy refreshments and a drop-in signing with the editor. Join us for brief remarks at 6pm.
That Directionless Light of the Future: Rediscovering Russell FitzGerald is the first major publication devoted to artist Russell FitzGerald. Bringing together newly commissioned scholarship and more than 90 reproductions of paintings, drawings, illustrations, archival material the book offers the first comprehensive account of an artist whose ambitious vision has remained hidden for decades.
Edited by Canadian art historian and curator Jon Davies, this handsome volume brings together reproductions of the artist’s work and other material with new texts by Davies, Dodie Bellamy, and Jamie Parra to return FitzGerald to art history and consider his relevance to the present.
For further information, visit our website.

item.description:

Hosted by York University Global Labour Research Centre (https://www.yorku.ca/research/glrc/)
In this talk, Katherine Nastovski revisits examples in Canadian labour movement history to ask what radical workers' education is not, and what separates initiatives that accommodate existing inequalities from those that help workers build collective power and solidarity across borders. She will offer a discussion prompt, followed by open conversation with participants.

item.title: Total Assault on Culture! FUGS FILM + NOVA '78: DOUBLE FEATURE — Sat Nov 28, 12:30 PM — Paradise Theatre
item.description:
Two films, one afternoon of radical music, art and New York counterculture.
Films We Like presents a special double feature of FUGS FILM and NOVA '78 at Paradise Theatre on November 28, featuring two Q&As with film critic Jason Gorber.
FUGS FILM, directed by Chuck Smith, chronicles The Fugs, the legendary 1960s underground rock band whose provocative music fused poetry, politics and anti-establishment rebellion.
NOVA '78, directed by Aaron Brookner and Rodrigo Areias, transports audiences to the legendary 1978 Nova Convention in New York City. Built from rediscovered archival footage, the film captures a remarkable gathering of countercultural icons including William S. Burroughs, Patti Smith, Frank Zappa, Allen Ginsberg and Laurie Anderson.
Join us for an afternoon celebrating the artists, musicians and troublemakers who helped reshape American culture.
Source: Toronto Events (Tockify)

item.title: A Short History of Library Architecture in Toronto and Beyond — Tue Dec 1, 6:30 PM — Toronto Reference Library
item.description:
Christopher Hume, the architecture critic and urban issues columnist of the Toronto Star, presents a short history of library architecture. He will be commenting on the structures and social relevance of monumental libraries from Paris, Boston, New York, with a focus on Toronto Public Libraries from around the city. Hume is the recipient of 2009 The National Newspaper Award for journalism in architecture and urban affairs. His illustrious career at the Toronto Star earned him a President’s Award for Architectural Journalism from the Royal Architectural Institute of Canada. Hume's book, William James’ Toronto Views, won a Toronto Heritage Award in 2000 and in 2004 he received a Landscape Ontario award.
Source: Toronto Public Library — Young Adults

item.title: Interactive Installations Tech Meetup Dec 2 — Wed Dec 2, 6:00 PM — TTLMakerspace
item.description:
Join the TTLMakerspace for a fun evening of creative tech and user experience design.
Responsive Installations: Using Sensors to Control the Visuals
Public installations come alive when they react to the people around them. In this three-hour workshop, you'll learn how to use sensors that detect motion, distance, touch and more to drive real-time animations.
This session bridges code and the physical world. Using a Raspberry Pi and p5.js, we'll wire up sensors, read their signals, and map them to visual parameters such as colour, motion and scale. By the end, you'll have a working responsive prototype, the practical skills to build work that responds to its audience, and a clear path to scaling it into a full installation.
What you'll learn:
- Wiring sensors to a Raspberry Pi's GPIO pins
- Sending sensor readings from the Pi into a p5.js sketch
- Mapping user interactions to animation and visuals
- Tips for making installations reliable in public spaces

item.description: Acoustic Harvest is delighted to present The Banjo Special, a unique concert experience featuring Arnie Naiman, Chris Coole, Brian Taheny, and Chris Quinn, four of Canada’s finest banjo players. This is not your ordinary banjo show. The Banjo Special takes the audience on a musical journey through the many lives of the banjo, from its early roots as an African gourd instrument, through early American traditions, old-time country music, rural blues, bluegrass, and all the way to Ireland. Each musician brings a different voice to the instrument. Arnie Naiman and Chris Coole are widely respected old-time clawhammer players, known for their deep feel, original tunes, and masterful command of traditional style. Brian Taheny, originally from Sligo, Ireland, brings the bright, driving energy of Irish tenor banjo. item.title: Zoning for Major Transit Station Areas – Public Information Session — Mon Dec 7, 6:30 PM — Online
item.description:
Project: Planning Study Community Consultation Meetings
Gladki Planning Associates, on behalf of the City of Toronto, is hosting a virtual Public Information Session about new zoning permissions around subway, GO and light rail transit (LRT) stations. As a result of a Provincial decision in August 2025, the City is adding permissions for more homes to be built near 120 transit stations across Toronto. These updates will affect parts of the city that are within about a 10-minute walk (500–800 metres) of subway stations, GO stations and LRT stops. Since fall 2025, City staff have been engaging interested and affected parties and working on the updates.
